title: FPS2's two open questions and alpha 2 round 2's tool cost, on BOATS at the graphics cap 60, tick cap 1000: (1) what a WORKING citizen costs -- FPS2's dwarves were idle (0 of 29 held a job; the fort had no stockpile) -- by giving the fort one stockpile that takes everything (cx-load work: every loose item becomes a hauling job), with and without +60 citizens; (2) tool off vs on in pairs (round 2's single reading: 126 vs 168 t/s); (3) a season (100,800 ticks) with all three caverns breached vs closed, so cavern life has time to use the shaft.
fork: Is a working dwarf, a season of open caverns, or the tool itself a cost comparable to a wild animal (~0.04 ms/tick each in FPS2)?

predictions.model: working dwarves cost more than idle ones
predictions.expects: W1 below W0, and W3-W1 larger than W2-W0

predictions.model: the tool is a small cost (FPS1: 0%)

predictions.expects: S3 falls below S0 in the later samples as cavern creatures come up

kill_criterion: a work arm whose working count is under 15 at its second sample did not put the fort to work; a breach arm whose walk line never reads true did not open the caverns
culling: the first sample step of every replicate (warm-up, load-time caches)
